popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus names Periboea (not Sophocles' Merope) as wife of Polybus and foster-mother of the exposed Oedipus — the Corinthian queen who raises the Theban foundling as her own.

popCulture.title: Periboea
popCulture.description: Queen of Corinth by Polybus — foster mother of Oedipus in the Apollodoran strand; Sophocles and many modern tellings call her Merope instead.

popCulture.title: Polybus of Corinth
popCulture.description: Periboea's husband — the childless king who adopts the infant from Cithaeron and whose supposed death frees Oedipus to walk toward Thebes.

popCulture.title: Oedipus Rex
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' tragedy keeps the Corinthian foster-parents at the plot's hinge — the gentle house Oedipus flees, though the queen's name there is Merope rather than Periboea.
